# Research: prompt route safety

**Spec**: [spec.md](spec.md) · **Plan**: [plan.md](plan.md) · **Tasks**: [tasks.md](tasks.md)

This feature hardens `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt`, the one API route that already
delivers free text into a running session. It is the route ai-lawnmower's `answer`
and opp-lease handoff call today, so every change here is a change to a live client.

## Where the evidence comes from

Three sources, and each decision below says which one it leans on.

| Tag | Source | Status |
|---|---|---|
| **Probe** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/ralph/plans/lm-steer-design/results.md`, numbered checks | Outside this repo, read-only. The checks this feature turns on are transcribed into `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` ("Probe results that decide this plan") because the loop that implements this spec cannot reach that path |
| **Design** | `~/code/ai-lawnmower/docs/mcp-session-steering-design.md`, section (g) "Phase 3 detail" | Outside this repo, read-only. It is where requirements 1 to 7 are stated |
| **Code** | This repository at `30941f3` | Read and re-read in tree on 10/14/26; the line references below were checked, not remembered |

The decisions were taken during planning, before any task ran, and are recorded in
`ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md` under "Decisions already
made". They are reproduced here with their evidence. **They are not reopened by the
implementation**; a task that finds one of them wrong stops and says so rather than
choosing differently.

## The route as it stands (Code, 10/14/26)

What the hardening is measured against:

- `internal/httpapi/sessions.go` `promptSession` (line 772) decodes `promptRequest`,
  best-effort-reads the pane for a known dialog (`paneDialogState`, which is
  additive information and never a gate), calls `Manager.Prompt`, and answers `202`
  with `{"id","delivered","parked_on","suspicious_dialog"}`.
- `refusePrompt` (line 849) maps `session.ErrEmptyPrompt` to `400` and **everything
  else to a `500` with no detail**. There is no 409 on this route today.
- `internal/session/manager.go` `Manager.Prompt` (line 1194) refuses an empty ID
  (`ErrSessionNotFound`), `StateDead` (`ErrSessionDead`) and empty text
  (`ErrEmptyPrompt`); takes `lockSession`; calls `m.paste`; then `SendKeys` Enter.
- `m.paste` (line 1253) is bracketed **only** when the harness spec says
  `BracketedPaste`, which Claude's does not (spec 019 D9 left that to spec 018, and
  spec 018 FR-006 declined it for the API door).
- `Manager.Prompt` does **not** read liveness, does **not** consult `StateFailed`,
  and does **not** take the restart claim.

So a prompt into a session whose Claude has exited lands in a login shell as a
command line, and a prompt racing a revival lands half in one process and half in
the next. Those are the two failures this feature closes.

---

## D1 Spec number

**Decision.** This feature is `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`.

**Evidence.** The design calls it "crswd spec 018", but `specs/018-interactive-input`
(the session page's input panel) and `specs/019-codex-runtime` already exist in this
repository (Code: `ls specs/`). 020 is the first free number.

The milestone directory keeps the design's name — `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/` —
because the lawnmower side refers to it that way. The mismatch is deliberate and is
stated in `VALIDATION_CONTRACT.md` so that a later reader does not "fix" one to match
the other.

---

## D2 Liveness gate (requirement 1)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` reads the session's row from the controller's `List`
and branches on its `Claude` liveness:

- `LivenessStopped` → refuse with `ErrSessionNotReady`, before any tmux command that
  changes anything.
- `LivenessUnknown` → deliver.
- `LivenessRunning` → deliver.
- A `List` that fails → an error, not a delivery.

The gate runs **twice**: once before the paste, and again after the paste and before
the Enter. If the second read is stopped, the daemon sends `C-u` and no Enter.

**Evidence.**

- Probe check 13: `@crswd-binary` matched `pane_current_command` on 6 of 6 live panes,
  three of them `rcq` panes. So the option the daemon already sets is a true liveness
  signal for the sessions lawnmower actually drives, not only for the plain case.
- Code: `tmuxctl.SessionInfo.Claude` is the three-valued `Liveness`
  (`internal/tmuxctl/controller.go:312-341`), derived from `@crswd-binary` against the
  pane's current command — by one tmux format in `Exec` (`exec.go:548`) and by
  `livenessOf` in the fake (`fake.go:251`). Both exist already; nothing new is
  measured here.
- Spec 012 FR-006 ("detect a session whose Claude process has stopped while its shell
  survives") is the requirement this reads, and `supervisor.go:153-156` already treats
  `LivenessUnknown` as healthy with a comment saying it must. This gate reads it the
  same way, so a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed keeps working.
- Probe check 1: there is no check-then-Enter race after the first turn; the lost-Enter
  window is the first ~5 s after launch, which is out of scope (D9). That is why two
  reads around the paste are enough and a third is not.

**Why `List` and not a new method.** A per-session liveness method on
`tmuxctl.Controller` would force a matching change in the k8s module's `podctl`
(Code: `k8s/` is a second module reaching the root's `internal/` through `replace ../`).
This milestone adds no `Controller` method, so `podctl` is untouched and the cluster
build does not move.

**Why the second read, and why `C-u`.** Between the paste and the Enter the pane can
fall back to a shell — Claude exits, the composer's text is gone, and the Enter would
submit whatever the paste left on the shell's line as a command. `C-u` clears that
line; sending no Enter means nothing runs. Refusing *after* a paste is not as good as
refusing before one, and the `C-u` is what makes the imperfect case harmless rather
than merely reported.

*Rejected: refusing `LivenessUnknown`.* It is the state of every session started by a
build older than the option, and refusing it would make this route stop working for
sessions the supervisor itself calls healthy — two answers to one question.

*Rejected: reading the pane's text to decide readiness.* Spec 012 FR-007 forbids it
for detection, pane content is secret under `docs/security.md` §3, and `paneDialogState`
already shows what a text read is good for: additive information, never a gate.

---

## D3 Not-ready answer (requirements 1, 2 and 5)

**Decision.** One new sentinel, `session.ErrSessionNotReady`. Every refusal this
feature adds inside `internal/session` returns it, and `refusePrompt` maps it to
`409` with body `{"error":"session not ready"}` and an audit **Deny** whose reason is
the constant `session not ready`.

A session in `StateFailed` gets it. `StateDead` keeps today's answer unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `StateFailed` (`internal/session/session.go:86`) means the supervisor tried to
  bring the session back and ran out of attempts (`supervisor.go:311-314`). Nothing is
  running in that pane, so a prompt into it is the same failure as a stopped pane;
  `Manager.Prompt` refuses `StateDead` today and says nothing about `StateFailed`.
- Code: a dead session is already refused as a `404` by the resolver before
  `promptSession` runs, and `refusePrompt`'s comment says reaching its `ErrSessionDead`
  branch would mean a record went terminal between two layers of one request. Leaving
  `dead` alone keeps that path exactly as it is and keeps the enumeration rule
  (`docs/security.md`: a session the caller may not have is a 404, never a 403/409).
- lawnmower's `deliver()` (`~/code/ai-lawnmower/loop/session_resume.py`, as recorded in
  PROGRESS.md on 10/14/26) treats **any** body carrying an `error` key as a refusal. So
  `409 {"error":"session not ready"}` reads as a refusal to the existing client with no
  client change, which is why the body carries `error` and not a new key.
- `docs/security.md` "Rate limiting & audit": every reason on the trail is a sentinel
  this codebase authored. `session not ready` is one. It names no state, no pane
  content and no prompt — an operator reading the trail learns that the route refused
  and why in the daemon's own words, and a caller learns nothing about the host it
  could not already see.

*Rejected: a sentinel per reason* (stopped pane, failed state, restart held). Three
sentinels reaching one status code with one body is three things to keep in step for
a distinction the caller cannot observe. The trail distinguishes nothing more here
because the three are the same event to the client: not now, try later.

*Rejected: `503`.* The condition is about one named session, not about this daemon's
capacity, and `409` is already the contract's "the host's state refuses this" code
(the unverified-teardown answer, `sessions.go:749`).

---

## D4 Bracketed paste (requirement 3)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` pastes with `PasteBracketed` for **every** harness.
`Manager.Compact` keeps its harness-based paste (`m.paste`). No newline refusal.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `Controller.PasteBracketed` already exists (spec 018 added it; `paste-buffer -p`,
  `internal/tmuxctl/exec.go:220-230`), and the session page's type route already uses it
  for every harness. This decision reuses that method; it adds none.
- `docs/security.md` §2: inside a bracketed paste the terminal does not interpret the
  pasted bytes, which is what makes multi-line text one paste instead of a line of text
  plus a submit plus another line. The same section already requires that caller text
  reach tmux only through `load-buffer` on stdin and then `paste-buffer`, bracketed on
  the session page's route; this extends the bracketing to the API door's route.
- Spec 019 D9 / research M3–M5 measured that Codex swallows the Enter after a *plain*
  paste and submits correctly after a bracketed one. Claude accepts both. So bracketed
  is the one form that is correct for both harnesses, and `Prompt` stops needing to ask
  which harness it is talking to at all.
**A consequence this decision does not close, named rather than smoothed over.**
`docs/security.md` §2 says text holding a C0 control other than TAB or LF is refused,
"because inside a bracketed paste `ESC[201~` would end the paste" — and that sentence
is about **the session page's route**. The refusal is `session.ValidateTyped`
(`internal/session/input.go:75-92`, spec 018 FR-004), and Code confirms it is called by
`Manager.Type` (`input.go:105`) and **not** by `Manager.Prompt`: the API door's
`promptRequest.Text` is validated only for emptiness and the body-size bound
(`internal/httpapi/sessions.go:264-270`, "that is the whole of its validation
(FR-030)"). So bracketing this route's paste makes a byte sequence relevant that was
inert under a plain paste: a caller that sent `\x1b[201~` mid-text would end the paste
early and the remainder would reach the pane as keystrokes rather than as pasted text.

D4 as decided adds no refusal, so this feature does not close it, and this document
does not invent one. What is recorded here is that the mechanism already exists
(`ValidateTyped`, one call away) and that spec.md has to say which way it goes —
either the route gains that check or the exposure is accepted in writing. It is logged
as a finding in `ralph/plans/lm-steer-crswd-018/PROGRESS.md` so the task that writes
spec.md cannot miss it. No measured client sends a control byte: every fixture in
PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures" is printable text plus newlines.

**Why no newline refusal.** The opp-lease handoff pastes multi-line item bodies
(Probe/Design: the builders in `console.py` and `lawnmower-route`, whose shapes are
fixed byte-for-byte as T011's fixtures in PROGRESS.md "Payload fixtures"). A rule
refusing `\n` would refuse the traffic this route exists to carry. Bracketing is what
makes a newline safe; refusing newlines would be the same protection obtained by
breaking the client.

**Why `Compact` is untouched.** Its payload is a daemon constant, not caller text, and
spec 018 FR-006's "unchanged" promise about this route is amended here only for what
requirements 1 to 6 name. Changing `Compact` as well would be an unrequested change to
a path with no requirement behind it (constitution IV).

This amends spec 018 **FR-006**, which says the API door's prompt route must be
unchanged — plain paste, then Enter, with bracketed paste reserved for the interactive
route. The amendment is recorded in spec.md, not left to this file.

---

## D5 Leading `!` or `/` (requirement 4)

**Decision.** On the **API door only**: refuse a prompt whose first character that is
not space, tab, CR or LF is `!` or `/`. The answer is `400` with the uniform
bad-request body, decided before any tmux command runs. The session page's type route
is unchanged.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 4: those two characters are Claude Code's slash-command and
  shell-escape prefixes. A prompt that begins with one is not a prompt — `/clear`
  discards the conversation the caller was trying to continue, and `!` runs a shell
  command in the session's own unsandboxed context. A client that meant to say
  something and instead silently reset the session is the failure being closed.
- Code grep of 10/14/26 over every lawnmower caller of this route: `console.py`
  `_answer_action` (via `session_resume.deliver`), `lawnmower-route` `resume_prompt`,
  `_batch_listing_prompt`, and `opp_followup_prompt` all build text whose first
  character is a letter. **No existing caller is refused by this rule.** That is the
  whole of why it can be added to a live route at all.
- The fixtures in PROGRESS.md keep the shape that matters: `resume.txt` holds a *later*
  line beginning `/compact`. The rule is about the first non-whitespace character of
  the whole text and nothing else, so that fixture is accepted. A rule scanning every
  line would refuse real traffic.
- The browser door is excluded because its route is the operator typing at their own
  session: `docs/security.md` records the session page's input panel as text or a key
  the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed it. An operator typing
  `/compact` into their own session is the feature, not a mistake, and T004 asserts
  that it still arrives.

*Rejected: stripping or escaping the leading character.* It would deliver something
the caller did not write, into a session that executes code. A refusal the client can
see and fix is strictly better than a silent rewrite.

*Rejected: an allowlist of safe slash commands.* The daemon would then own a list that
tracks Claude Code's command set, and a stale list is a command delivered because
nobody updated a table. The route carries prompts; a caller that wants a command has
the browser door and the operator behind it.

This amends spec 018 **FR-006** a second time (see D4): the route gains one refusal
the interactive route does not have.

---

## D6 Lock and buffer (requirement 5)

**Decision.** `Manager.Prompt` takes the restart claim (`claimRestart`, non-blocking)
**after** `lockSession`, refuses with `ErrSessionNotReady` when a revive or a continue
already holds it, and releases it on return.

**Evidence.**

- Code: `lockSession` (`internal/session/input.go`) is already the per-session mutex
  shared by Type, PressKey, Prompt, Compact, SetMode, Continue, Destroy and the
  supervisor's Codex discovery. `Prompt` already takes it (`manager.go:1209`), so two
  concurrent prompts already cannot interleave paste and Enter.
- Code: `Exec.paste` already draws a fresh buffer name per paste (`newBufferName`,
  `exec.go:186-195`, 16 random hex digits behind `BufferPrefix`, "per call rather than
  per session, so a second paste into the same session cannot overwrite the first
  one's text before it lands"). The fake records the names through `nextBuffer`, so a
  test can assert they differ. Both halves of requirement 5's "distinct buffers, no
  interleaving" are therefore **already true**, from the spec 018 and 019 review
  passes, and this feature only has to prove it (T010) rather than build it.
- Code: `claimRestart` / `releaseRestart` (`manager.go:2674-2688`) are non-blocking and
  are what revival and continue hold while they type a new command line into the pane.
  That is the one concurrent writer `lockSession` does **not** exclude, because a
  restart does not hold the session lock for its whole run. A prompt pasted into a pane
  mid-restart lands partly in the dying process and partly on the shell the new command
  line is about to be typed at.

**Why non-blocking.** A prompt that waited for a revival would hold an HTTP request
open across a process restart, and the caller cannot tell a slow delivery from a lost
one. `409 session not ready` is a fact the client can act on now; lawnmower's
`deliver()` already reads it as a refusal (D3).

**Why after `lockSession` and not before.** The two are taken in one order everywhere
or they deadlock. `lockSession` first matches `Continue`'s order, so no new ordering
rule enters the package.

---

## D7 `request_id` (requirement 6)

**Decision.** The prompt body gains one optional field, `request_id`: 1 to 32
characters of `[a-z0-9-]`. A value outside that is a `400`. A valid value is echoed in
the `202` body and written as `request_id` on the request's one audit record. Absent
means the field appears nowhere — not in the response, not on the record.

**Evidence.**

- Design, requirement 6: the caller needs to correlate a delivery it made with the
  record of that delivery, across a daemon restart and without a transcript. The audit
  trail is the only durable record of a prompt, and today it carries nothing the caller
  chose.
- Code: `audit.Record` (`internal/audit/audit.go:390-414`) has Action, Caller,
  SessionID, Decision, Reason and Remote. `RequestAudit`
  (`internal/httpapi/middleware.go`) has `SetSessionID` and `Deny`, so the
  carry-it-onto-the-one-record mechanism exists and gains one setter (T002) rather
  than a second record.
- The value goes in a **field of its own** and never into `Reason`. `Record.Reason`'s
  own documentation forbids caller-supplied text in it ("must never be built from
  caller-supplied text, a prompt, pane output, a token, or the shared secret"), and
  that rule is unamended: `Reason` stays server-authored sentinels, and `request_id`
  is the one field on the record whose bytes the caller chose.
- `docs/security.md` §2 and the decoder it shows: the body is decoded into a typed
  struct with `DisallowUnknownFields`, so the field has to be declared to be accepted
  at all, and anything else in the body is still refused.

**Why that alphabet and that length.** The field is written to an audit record that an
operator reads and a tool greps. Lower-case, digits and `-` is the same shape this
repository already holds session names to (`^[a-zA-Z0-9-]{1,64}$`, `docs/security.md`
§2), minus the upper case; 32 characters fits a ULID or a UUID and leaves nothing for
a caller to smuggle. Validation is at the boundary and the refusal is a `400`, so no
tmux command runs for a body that was never going to be accepted.

**Why this is not a hole in FR-042.** Spec 001 FR-042 forbids prompt text, session
output, credentials and the shared secret on an audit record, and nothing in it
contemplated a caller-chosen correlation value. This amends FR-042 for **this one
field**, and the bound is exact: the record gains the `request_id` the caller sent and
**nothing about the prompt** — not its text, not its length, not a hash of it. The
alphabet is what keeps the field from becoming a channel for the text itself: 32 bytes
of `[a-z0-9-]` cannot carry a prompt, and a caller that tried would be writing a value
an operator can see is not an identifier. The amendment is recorded in spec.md.

---

## D8 Registry gate (requirement 7) — deferred, not a clarification

**Decision.** Requirement 7, a readiness gate reading Claude Code's session registry,
is **out of scope** for this feature. It is listed under Out of scope in spec.md with
this reason. It is **not** an open question in constitution II's sense — a deferred
MAY is a decision, and the marker that principle calls for is deliberately absent
from this directory. (Spelling that marker out here would also trip the gate that
greps this directory for it, which is why no file under `specs/020-prompt-route-safety/`
contains the phrase.)

**Evidence.**

- The design states requirement 7 as a **MAY**, not a MUST. Deferring a MAY is a scope
  decision, not an unanswered question, and constitution II is about requirements that
  are *ambiguous* — this one is clear and declined.
- Probe check 8 left open whether crswd can read `sessions/<pid>.json` at all under
  spec 017's v2 option B. No FR in spec 017 places that file in a pod, so a gate built
  on it would work on the VM and silently do nothing in the cluster — a readiness check
  that is right about one deployment and blind in the other.
- Probe checks 3 and 9: the registry misses the trust dialog and misses a half-typed
  draft in the composer. So it answers "a session exists" and not "this session will
  read what I send next", which is the question requirement 7 was asked to answer.
- The liveness gate (D2) is the part of requirement 1 that is measurable with what the
  daemon already holds, and it is what ships.

**What this costs, stated rather than smoothed over.** A session sitting on a dialog
still accepts a prompt; `paneDialogState` already reports that in the `202`
(`parked_on`, `suspicious_dialog`) and still does not refuse. That limit is the same
one spec 018 recorded, and closing it needs a readiness signal this daemon does not
have yet.

Also out of this feature by the same reasoning: **the Go code never opens a Claude
transcript or a `~/.claude/sessions/*.json` registry file.** Spec 013 FR-025 is
unchanged by this feature, and spec 019 D11's bounded Codex rollout read stays the
single exception it already is.

---

## D9 Out of scope

**Decision.** This feature does not do any of the following, and a task that finds
itself needing one stops rather than widening:

| Not done here | Why |
|---|---|
| Opening a transcript | Spec 013 FR-025 (D8) |
| Holding or calling an LLM | The daemon routes keystrokes; it does not reason about them |
| A seventh API route | The API door has exactly six (Code: `internal/httpapi/server.go`'s route switch; six `## <METHOD> <path>` headings in `specs/001-crswd-daemon-core/contracts/http-api.md`). Requirements 1 to 6 are all changes to one existing route |
| Free text on the browser door beyond spec 018 | Spec 018 owns that panel; D5 touches its route only to assert it is unchanged |
| The startup lost-Enter window | Probe check 1b: an Enter can be lost in the first ~5 s after launch. Two liveness reads around the paste do not see it, and closing it needs a start-up readiness signal (D8) |
| The socket transport | The probe's verdict ("flip to socket") binds the lm-steer-write milestone, not this one |
| A new package under `internal/` | Every change lands in `audit`, `httpapi`, `session` or `tmuxctl` |

The last two rows are also hard rules of the loop that implements this spec, and the
validation contract asserts the `internal/` one by diffing the tree against `main`.

---

## Not verified

Stated so that a later reader does not mistake any of these for a settled fact:

- Whether a pane can fall back to a shell *between* the second liveness read and the
  Enter. The window is two tmux commands wide and nothing measured it; the `C-u` of D2
  covers the measured case (an exit during the paste) and not this one.
- Whether `LivenessUnknown` ever appears for a session this daemon created. It is
  reachable only for a session created before `@crswd-binary` existed, and no such
  session was on the probe host.
- What a Codex session does with a prompt refused after its paste. `C-u` clears a
  Claude composer and a shell line; Codex's composer was not measured against it.
- Whether any non-lawnmower client of this route exists. The grep covered ai-lawnmower
  only, so D5's "no existing caller is refused" is a statement about that client.

3	What "done" means for this milestone, decided before the plan was cut. A checker

24	
25	- A prompt to a session whose pane has fallen back to a shell answers `409` `{"error":"session not ready"}` and no paste reaches the pane: `go test ./internal/... -run 'Prompt'` exits 0.

1	# Feature Specification: Interactive Input on the Session Page
2	
3	**Feature Branch**: `plan/interactive-input`
4	**Created**: 2026-10-06
5	**Status**: Draft
6	**Input**: Operator (Craig), 2026-10-05: "enabling input when we click on a
7	specific session … regardless of whether it's Claude or Codex … being able to go
8	back in the history is probably something that would be kind of important."
9	Option chosen by the operator on 2026-10-06: **a prompt box, a key bar and a
10	scrollback viewer**. No terminal emulator, no WebSocket, no new dependency.
11	
12	This is the surface spec 003 deferred by name (`specs/003-dashboard-actions/spec.md:223`:
13	"a general 'type into the session' control is a larger surface with its own
14	questions and is not part of it"). Those questions are answered below.
15	
16	## Open for the operator
17	
18	**NEEDS CLARIFICATION: none blocking.** Every decision is made in `research.md`
19	with the rejected alternative beside it. Two questions can only be answered on a
20	phone, and ship UNANSWERED with fallbacks named in advance (FR-021):
21	
22	- **Q4**: does the key bar reach every key in portrait, without horizontal scroll?
23	- **Q5**: with the soft keyboard up, are the textarea and Send still on screen?
24	
25	## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*
26	
27	### User Story 1 - Type a message into a session from the browser (Priority: P1)
28	
29	The operator opens a session and types a reply, a multi-line prompt or a slash
30	command into a text box, and sends it. This works the same for Claude Code and
31	Codex, because the daemon delivers bytes and knows nothing about either program.
32	
33	**Independent Test**: Open a live session's page, type `hello` and press Send.
34	Within 2s the pane shows the session working on `hello`.
35	
36	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
37	
38	1. **Given** a live session the operator owns, **When** they type text and press
39	   **Send**, **Then** the text reaches the pane by bracketed paste followed by one
40	   Enter. The request answers `204`, and the textarea is cleared.
41	2. **Given** a textarea holding two lines, **When** the operator presses "Send",
42	   **Then** the program receives one two-line message. It does not submit after
43	   line one. (This was measured; see research.md R1.)
44	3. **Given** text in the textarea, **When** the operator presses "Type only",
45	   **Then** the text reaches the program's input box and no Enter is pressed.
46	4. **Given** the textarea has focus on a desktop, **When** the operator presses
47	   Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter, **Then** this does what Send does. A plain Enter inserts
48	   a newline.
49	5. **Given** empty text, or text holding a control character, or text over 16384
50	   bytes, **When** it is sent, **Then** nothing reaches the pane. The toast says
51	   which rule refused it.
52	6. **Given** a session that is gone or is not the caller's, **When** text is sent,
53	   **Then** the answer is the uniform not-found every action gives.
54	
55	### User Story 2 - Press the keys a phone keyboard does not have (Priority: P1)
56	
57	The operator answers a menu, interrupts a turn, or cycles Claude Code's mode
58	(Shift+Tab) from a phone, where the soft keyboard has no Esc, Ctrl, Tab or arrow
59	keys.
60	
61	**Independent Test**: Open a session sitting on a numbered menu. Tap "↓" then
62	**Enter** and see the second option chosen.
63	
64	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
65	
66	1. **Given** a live session, **When** the operator taps a key-bar button, **Then**
67	   exactly that key reaches the pane once, and the request answers `204`.
68	2. **Given** a POST naming a key outside the allowlist, **When** it arrives,
69	   **Then** nothing reaches the pane, and the outcome is `key-unknown`.
70	3. **Given** a phone in portrait at 390px wide, **When** the session page renders,
71	   **Then** every key-bar button is at least `--tap` (44px) tall, and the bar
72	   wraps instead of scrolling sideways.
73	
74	### User Story 3 - Read what scrolled off the screen (Priority: P2)
75	
76	The operator opens "Scrollback" under the pane and reads the session's history,
77	which tmux keeps but the live pane never showed.
78	
79	**Independent Test**: In a session that has printed 3000 lines, open Scrollback.
80	Line 1 of the 3000 is readable.
81	
82	**Acceptance Scenarios**:
83	
84	1. **Given** a session page, **When** it renders, **Then** a closed
85	   `<details>` labelled "Scrollback" sits under the input panel, and no history
86	   is fetched.
87	2. **Given** the disclosure is opened, **When** it opens, **Then** the page fetches
88	   `GET /sessions/{id}/history` and shows up to 5000 lines of history as text, with
89	   ANSI stripped. The history does not include the visible screen, which the pane
90	   above already shows.
91	3. **Given** the disclosure is closed and opened again, **When** it opens, **Then**
92	   the history is fetched again.
93	4. **Given** a session with no history yet, **When** the disclosure opens, **Then**
94	   it reads "No scrollback yet." and is not an empty box.
95	5. **Given** a session created before this feature, **When** its history is read,
96	   **Then** it has tmux's old 2000-line limit. Only new sessions get 5000.
97	
98	### Edge Cases
99	
100	- **A session parked on a dialog** (trust prompt, `/rc` menu, Codex update
101	  prompt): input is not gated. The key bar exists to answer exactly these. The
102	  dialog heuristic (`session.DetectDialog`) keeps reporting and never refuses.
103	  One such dialog is dangerous to answer blind: Codex's "Update available" menu,
104	  where Enter on the default starts a global `npm install` (research.md R8).
105	  Spec 019 prevents it at launch with `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false`;
106	  this spec does not gate input on it.
107	- **A program in the alternate screen** (a pager, `vim`, Codex without
108	  `--no-alt-screen`): tmux keeps no history for it. The scrollback reads "No
109	  scrollback yet." and says nothing false. Spec 019 starts Codex with
110	  `--no-alt-screen`, measured `alternate_on=0`.
111	- **A text payload containing `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`** (the end-of-paste marker) would end
112	  the bracketed paste early and turn the rest of the payload into keystrokes.
113	  FR-004 refuses every C0 control except LF and TAB, so this payload cannot arrive.
114	- **A browser sends CRLF from a textarea**: the handler normalises `\r\n` to `\n`
115	  before validation (FR-004). A bare `\r` left after that is a control character
116	  and is refused.
117	- **Two tabs typing into one session**: both deliveries land, one after the
118	  other. `Manager` holds one mutex per session across a whole delivery (a paste
119	  and its Enter, or one key), so a key can never land inside another message's
120	  text. Each paste also loads its own tmux buffer, `crswd-in-` plus 16 random
121	  hex, so two pastes cannot overwrite each other, and a paste that fails deletes
122	  its buffer.
123	- **A burst of key presses** past the budget: refused with `input-limited` and
124	  nothing delivered. The budget refills at 4 a second.
125	- **History larger than the bound** (impossible at `history-limit 5000` with
126	  `-S -5000 -E -1`, but a tmux that answers differently): `CaptureHistory`
127	  refuses with `ErrHistoryTooLarge` and the route answers `500` with no body.
128	  Truncation is never used.
129	- **No script running**: the textarea and key bar are ordinary forms. A `204`
130	  leaves the browser on the page. A refusal lands on the fleet page with the
131	  outcome banner, like every other action. Scrollback needs script, and without
132	  script its body says "Scrollback needs JavaScript." (FR-014).
133	
134	## Requirements *(mandatory)*
135	
136	### The rule this feature amends
137	
138	- **FR-001**: The rule "it never types into a working session" (`AGENTS.md:10`)
139	  MUST be amended to read exactly: *"The daemon never types into a working session
140	  on its own initiative. The one exception is the session page's input panel
141	  (spec 018): text or a key the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed
142	  it."* `docs/security.md` §2 MUST carry the same rule. The daemon MUST still
143	  never type into a session from a timer, a supervisor, a dialog detector or any
144	  path without an operator request behind it.
145	
146	### Delivery
147	
148	- **FR-002**: `POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/type` MUST read form fields `text`
149	  and `enter`. It MUST deliver `text` with `tmux load-buffer` (payload on stdin)
150	  then `tmux paste-buffer -p -d` (bracketed). If `enter` is exactly `yes`, it MUST
151	  then send the `Enter` key. Any other value of `enter` means no Enter.
152	- **FR-003**: `POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/key` MUST read form field `key`, map
153	  it through the daemon's allowlist (FR-005) to a tmux key name, and send that
154	  constant with `tmux send-keys`. Caller bytes MUST never reach a `send-keys`
155	  argv.
156	- **FR-004**: The handler MUST replace every `\r\n` in `text` with `\n`. It MUST
157	  then refuse text that is empty, longer than 16384 bytes, not valid UTF-8, or
158	  holding any byte in `0x00–0x1F` other than `0x09` and `0x0A`, or `0x7F`. The
159	  manager MUST make the same checks again.
160	- **FR-005**: The key allowlist is exactly these twelve symbolic names, mapped to
161	  these tmux names: `enter→Enter`, `escape→Escape`, `interrupt→C-c`, `tab→Tab`,
162	  `backtab→BTab`, `up→Up`, `down→Down`, `left→Left`, `right→Right`,
163	  `pageup→PageUp`, `pagedown→PageDown`, `backspace→BSpace`. Measured on tmux 3.4,
164	  each produces the expected byte sequence (research.md R3).
165	- **FR-006**: The API door's `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt` MUST be unchanged:
166	  plain paste, then Enter. Bracketed paste is for the interactive route only.
167	
168	### Gates
169	
170	- **FR-007**: Both POST routes MUST be registered with `handleAction`. That means
171	  layer 1, then `Sec-Fetch-Site` same-origin with an absent header refused, then
172	  the page token, then `MaxBytesReader`, all before the handler runs.
173	- **FR-008**: Both POST routes MUST resolve the session with `Manager.View(id,
174	  operator.Owner)` and answer every lookup failure with `notFoundAction`, the
175	  uniform not-found.
176	- **FR-009**: Both POST routes MUST spend one token from one shared per-operator
177	  bucket (`inputs`, keyed by `auth.CallerID`, 240 per minute, burst 120) before
178	  the lookup. A refused spend MUST answer outcome `input-limited` and deliver
179	  nothing.
180	- **FR-010**: A successful type or key MUST answer `204 No Content` with no body.
181	  Every refusal after the gate MUST answer `303` to the fleet page with the
182	  route's outcome code, as every other action does. When the paste lands and the
183	  Enter after it fails, the outcome is `type-unsubmitted` ("The text was typed
184	  but not submitted"), not `type-failed`, and the script clears the textarea for
185	  it so a retry cannot type the text twice.
186	- **FR-011**: Type and key MUST move the session's last-driven clock with
187	  `store.Touch` once the delivery has succeeded (review #3: a failed delivery
188	  must not make a vanished session look driven); before it they only confirm the
189	  record is still in the store. A delivery that fails MUST ask the controller
190	  `Has` for the session, and an absent one answers `ErrSessionDead`, which the
191	  handlers turn into the uniform not-found. History MUST NOT move the clock.
192	
193	### Audit
194	
195	- **FR-012**: Each request MUST produce exactly one audit record, under the new
196	  actions `dashboard.type`, `dashboard.key` and `dashboard.history`. A record MUST
197	  carry no typed text, no key name and no history. The record shape is frozen
198	  (FR-016 of spec 003), so there is no field to put a key name in, and the leak
199	  suite MUST prove the text never appears.
200	
201	### Scrollback
202	
203	- **FR-013**: Every tmux session this daemon creates MUST be created with
204	  `history-limit 5000`. That means one tmux invocation,
205	  `tmux set-option -g history-limit 5000 ; new-session -d -s <name> -c <dir>`, with
206	  `;` as its own argv element. A per-session `set-option` after `new-session` does
207	  not change an existing pane's limit (measured, research.md R2).
208	- **FR-014**: `GET /sessions/{id}/history` MUST be registered with
209	  `handleBrowser`, refuse a cross-site request as the stream does
210	  (`crossSite`, `internal/httpapi/stream.go:464`), resolve with `View`, and answer
211	  `200 text/plain; charset=utf-8` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The body is the
212	  output of `tmux capture-pane -p -S -5000 -E -1`, passed through `tmuxctl.Strip`.
213	- **FR-015**: `CaptureHistory` MUST refuse, never truncate, output over 5000 lines
214	  or over 4 MiB, with `ErrHistoryTooLarge`. The route MUST answer that with `500`
215	  and no body.
216	- **FR-016**: The page MUST fetch history only when the Scrollback disclosure
217	  opens. It MUST fetch again on every open, and MUST put the answer into a
218	  `<pre class="pane">` with `textContent`. An empty answer MUST render "No
219	  scrollback yet."
220	
221	### Interface
222	
223	- **FR-017**: The input panel, the key bar and the Scrollback disclosure MUST be
224	  rendered inside `partials/pane.html`, after the pane's notes, only when the
225	  pane has a page token (`{{ with .PageToken }}`). They MUST use only `.button`,
226	  `.field-label`, `.field-input` and the new classes `.input-panel`, `.type-form`,
227	  `.key-bar`, `.scrollback`, `.scrollback-summary`.
228	- **FR-018**: On a coarse pointer, every key-bar button MUST be at least
229	  `var(--tap)` in both dimensions, and the textarea font MUST be `var(--fs-input)`.
230	  The key bar MUST be `flex-wrap: wrap`. No new width breakpoint is allowed
231	  (`TestTheDashboardHasExactlyOneBreakpoint`).
232	- **FR-019**: The textarea MUST carry `autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off"
233	  spellcheck="false"` and a `<label>`. The `.input-panel` MUST be
234	  `position: sticky; inset-block-end: 0`, so it stays on screen while the pane
235	  scrolls.
236	- **FR-020**: The pane note MUST read exactly: "This is the live screen, not
237	  scrollback. Open Scrollback below to read what came before it." The phrase "not
238	  scrollback" is pinned by two existing tests.
239	- **FR-021**: `docs/mobile-open-questions.md` MUST gain Q4 and Q5, both
240	  **UNANSWERED**, each with its fallback named. Q4 fallback: the key bar becomes a
241	  second `<details>` ("More keys") holding the arrows, PageUp/PageDown and
242	  Backspace, with Enter, Esc, Ctrl-C, Tab and Shift-Tab left visible. Q5 fallback:
243	  move the input panel above the pane.
244	
245	### Not in this feature
246	
247	- **FR-022**: No WebSocket, terminal emulator, vendored JavaScript, CSP change,
248	  API-door input route or change to the stream's 1s cadence. Each one is a
249	  separate decision with its own review. research.md R6 records why.
250	
251	**Key Entities**: **Key**, a symbolic name from FR-005's closed set. **Typed
252	text**, operator bytes that are secret under `docs/security.md` §3, exactly like
253	prompt text. **History**, the stripped text of tmux's scrollback for one pane,
254	excluding the visible screen.
255	
256	## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*
257	
258	- **SC-001**: `go test ./internal/tmuxctl -tags tmux -run 'Bracketed|History'`
259	  proves on a real tmux that a two-line bracketed paste arrives wrapped in
260	  `ESC[200~ … ESC[201~`, and that a 6000-line job yields at most 5000 lines of
261	  history from a session created by `Exec.New`.
262	- **SC-002**: The leak suite (`go test ./internal/audit -run Leak`) drives
263	  `dashboard.type` with a canary string, and the canary appears in no audit
264	  record and no log line.
265	- **SC-003**: Every refusal shape that `TestRefusalIsNotARedirect` applies to an
266	  action is applied to both input routes, and each answers its uniform status.
267	- **SC-004**: Disabling either route's registration fails a handler test.
268	- **SC-005**: Q4 and Q5 exist in `docs/mobile-open-questions.md` marked
269	  UNANSWERED, and nothing in this plan marks them answered.

# Feature Specification: Interactive Input on the Session Page

**Feature Branch**: `plan/interactive-input`
**Created**: 2026-10-06
**Status**: Draft
**Input**: Operator (Craig), 2026-10-05: "enabling input when we click on a
specific session … regardless of whether it's Claude or Codex … being able to go
back in the history is probably something that would be kind of important."
Option chosen by the operator on 2026-10-06: **a prompt box, a key bar and a
scrollback viewer**. No terminal emulator, no WebSocket, no new dependency.

This is the surface spec 003 deferred by name (`specs/003-dashboard-actions/spec.md:223`:
"a general 'type into the session' control is a larger surface with its own
questions and is not part of it"). Those questions are answered below.

## Open for the operator

**NEEDS CLARIFICATION: none blocking.** Every decision is made in `research.md`
with the rejected alternative beside it. Two questions can only be answered on a
phone, and ship UNANSWERED with fallbacks named in advance (FR-021):

- **Q4**: does the key bar reach every key in portrait, without horizontal scroll?
- **Q5**: with the soft keyboard up, are the textarea and Send still on screen?

## User Scenarios & Testing *(mandatory)*

### User Story 1 - Type a message into a session from the browser (Priority: P1)

The operator opens a session and types a reply, a multi-line prompt or a slash
command into a text box, and sends it. This works the same for Claude Code and
Codex, because the daemon delivers bytes and knows nothing about either program.

**Independent Test**: Open a live session's page, type `hello` and press Send.
Within 2s the pane shows the session working on `hello`.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a live session the operator owns, **When** they type text and press
   **Send**, **Then** the text reaches the pane by bracketed paste followed by one
   Enter. The request answers `204`, and the textarea is cleared.
2. **Given** a textarea holding two lines, **When** the operator presses "Send",
   **Then** the program receives one two-line message. It does not submit after
   line one. (This was measured; see research.md R1.)
3. **Given** text in the textarea, **When** the operator presses "Type only",
   **Then** the text reaches the program's input box and no Enter is pressed.
4. **Given** the textarea has focus on a desktop, **When** the operator presses
   Ctrl+Enter or Cmd+Enter, **Then** this does what Send does. A plain Enter inserts
   a newline.
5. **Given** empty text, or text holding a control character, or text over 16384
   bytes, **When** it is sent, **Then** nothing reaches the pane. The toast says
   which rule refused it.
6. **Given** a session that is gone or is not the caller's, **When** text is sent,
   **Then** the answer is the uniform not-found every action gives.

### User Story 2 - Press the keys a phone keyboard does not have (Priority: P1)

The operator answers a menu, interrupts a turn, or cycles Claude Code's mode
(Shift+Tab) from a phone, where the soft keyboard has no Esc, Ctrl, Tab or arrow
keys.

**Independent Test**: Open a session sitting on a numbered menu. Tap "↓" then
**Enter** and see the second option chosen.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a live session, **When** the operator taps a key-bar button, **Then**
   exactly that key reaches the pane once, and the request answers `204`.
2. **Given** a POST naming a key outside the allowlist, **When** it arrives,
   **Then** nothing reaches the pane, and the outcome is `key-unknown`.
3. **Given** a phone in portrait at 390px wide, **When** the session page renders,
   **Then** every key-bar button is at least `--tap` (44px) tall, and the bar
   wraps instead of scrolling sideways.

### User Story 3 - Read what scrolled off the screen (Priority: P2)

The operator opens "Scrollback" under the pane and reads the session's history,
which tmux keeps but the live pane never showed.

**Independent Test**: In a session that has printed 3000 lines, open Scrollback.
Line 1 of the 3000 is readable.

**Acceptance Scenarios**:

1. **Given** a session page, **When** it renders, **Then** a closed
   `<details>` labelled "Scrollback" sits under the input panel, and no history
   is fetched.
2. **Given** the disclosure is opened, **When** it opens, **Then** the page fetches
   `GET /sessions/{id}/history` and shows up to 5000 lines of history as text, with
   ANSI stripped. The history does not include the visible screen, which the pane
   above already shows.
3. **Given** the disclosure is closed and opened again, **When** it opens, **Then**
   the history is fetched again.
4. **Given** a session with no history yet, **When** the disclosure opens, **Then**
   it reads "No scrollback yet." and is not an empty box.
5. **Given** a session created before this feature, **When** its history is read,
   **Then** it has tmux's old 2000-line limit. Only new sessions get 5000.

### Edge Cases

- **A session parked on a dialog** (trust prompt, `/rc` menu, Codex update
  prompt): input is not gated. The key bar exists to answer exactly these. The
  dialog heuristic (`session.DetectDialog`) keeps reporting and never refuses.
  One such dialog is dangerous to answer blind: Codex's "Update available" menu,
  where Enter on the default starts a global `npm install` (research.md R8).
  Spec 019 prevents it at launch with `-c check_for_update_on_startup=false`;
  this spec does not gate input on it.
- **A program in the alternate screen** (a pager, `vim`, Codex without
  `--no-alt-screen`): tmux keeps no history for it. The scrollback reads "No
  scrollback yet." and says nothing false. Spec 019 starts Codex with
  `--no-alt-screen`, measured `alternate_on=0`.
- **A text payload containing `ESC [ 2 0 1 ~`** (the end-of-paste marker) would end
  the bracketed paste early and turn the rest of the payload into keystrokes.
  FR-004 refuses every C0 control except LF and TAB, so this payload cannot arrive.
- **A browser sends CRLF from a textarea**: the handler normalises `\r\n` to `\n`
  before validation (FR-004). A bare `\r` left after that is a control character
  and is refused.
- **Two tabs typing into one session**: both deliveries land, one after the
  other. `Manager` holds one mutex per session across a whole delivery (a paste
  and its Enter, or one key), so a key can never land inside another message's
  text. Each paste also loads its own tmux buffer, `crswd-in-` plus 16 random
  hex, so two pastes cannot overwrite each other, and a paste that fails deletes
  its buffer.
- **A burst of key presses** past the budget: refused with `input-limited` and
  nothing delivered. The budget refills at 4 a second.
- **History larger than the bound** (impossible at `history-limit 5000` with
  `-S -5000 -E -1`, but a tmux that answers differently): `CaptureHistory`
  refuses with `ErrHistoryTooLarge` and the route answers `500` with no body.
  Truncation is never used.
- **No script running**: the textarea and key bar are ordinary forms. A `204`
  leaves the browser on the page. A refusal lands on the fleet page with the
  outcome banner, like every other action. Scrollback needs script, and without
  script its body says "Scrollback needs JavaScript." (FR-014).

## Requirements *(mandatory)*

### The rule this feature amends

- **FR-001**: The rule "it never types into a working session" (`AGENTS.md:10`)
  MUST be amended to read exactly: *"The daemon never types into a working session
  on its own initiative. The one exception is the session page's input panel
  (spec 018): text or a key the operator sent, delivered once, when they pressed
  it."* `docs/security.md` §2 MUST carry the same rule. The daemon MUST still
  never type into a session from a timer, a supervisor, a dialog detector or any
  path without an operator request behind it.

### Delivery

- **FR-002**: `POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/type` MUST read form fields `text`
  and `enter`. It MUST deliver `text` with `tmux load-buffer` (payload on stdin)
  then `tmux paste-buffer -p -d` (bracketed). If `enter` is exactly `yes`, it MUST
  then send the `Enter` key. Any other value of `enter` means no Enter.
- **FR-003**: `POST /dashboard/sessions/{id}/key` MUST read form field `key`, map
  it through the daemon's allowlist (FR-005) to a tmux key name, and send that
  constant with `tmux send-keys`. Caller bytes MUST never reach a `send-keys`
  argv.
- **FR-004**: The handler MUST replace every `\r\n` in `text` with `\n`. It MUST
  then refuse text that is empty, longer than 16384 bytes, not valid UTF-8, or
  holding any byte in `0x00–0x1F` other than `0x09` and `0x0A`, or `0x7F`. The
  manager MUST make the same checks again.
- **FR-005**: The key allowlist is exactly these twelve symbolic names, mapped to
  these tmux names: `enter→Enter`, `escape→Escape`, `interrupt→C-c`, `tab→Tab`,
  `backtab→BTab`, `up→Up`, `down→Down`, `left→Left`, `right→Right`,
  `pageup→PageUp`, `pagedown→PageDown`, `backspace→BSpace`. Measured on tmux 3.4,
  each produces the expected byte sequence (research.md R3).
- **FR-006**: The API door's `POST /sessions/{id}/prompt` MUST be unchanged:
  plain paste, then Enter. Bracketed paste is for the interactive route only.

### Gates

- **FR-007**: Both POST routes MUST be registered with `handleAction`. That means
  layer 1, then `Sec-Fetch-Site` same-origin with an absent header refused, then
  the page token, then `MaxBytesReader`, all before the handler runs.
- **FR-008**: Both POST routes MUST resolve the session with `Manager.View(id,
  operator.Owner)` and answer every lookup failure with `notFoundAction`, the
  uniform not-found.
- **FR-009**: Both POST routes MUST spend one token from one shared per-operator
  bucket (`inputs`, keyed by `auth.CallerID`, 240 per minute, burst 120) before
  the lookup. A refused spend MUST answer outcome `input-limited` and deliver
  nothing.
- **FR-010**: A successful type or key MUST answer `204 No Content` with no body.
  Every refusal after the gate MUST answer `303` to the fleet page with the
  route's outcome code, as every other action does. When the paste lands and the
  Enter after it fails, the outcome is `type-unsubmitted` ("The text was typed
  but not submitted"), not `type-failed`, and the script clears the textarea for
  it so a retry cannot type the text twice.
- **FR-011**: Type and key MUST move the session's last-driven clock with
  `store.Touch` once the delivery has succeeded (review #3: a failed delivery
  must not make a vanished session look driven); before it they only confirm the
  record is still in the store. A delivery that fails MUST ask the controller
  `Has` for the session, and an absent one answers `ErrSessionDead`, which the
  handlers turn into the uniform not-found. History MUST NOT move the clock.

### Audit

- **FR-012**: Each request MUST produce exactly one audit record, under the new
  actions `dashboard.type`, `dashboard.key` and `dashboard.history`. A record MUST
  carry no typed text, no key name and no history. The record shape is frozen
  (FR-016 of spec 003), so there is no field to put a key name in, and the leak
  suite MUST prove the text never appears.

### Scrollback

- **FR-013**: Every tmux session this daemon creates MUST be created with
  `history-limit 5000`. That means one tmux invocation,
  `tmux set-option -g history-limit 5000 ; new-session -d -s <name> -c <dir>`, with
  `;` as its own argv element. A per-session `set-option` after `new-session` does
  not change an existing pane's limit (measured, research.md R2).
- **FR-014**: `GET /sessions/{id}/history` MUST be registered with
  `handleBrowser`, refuse a cross-site request as the stream does
  (`crossSite`, `internal/httpapi/stream.go:464`), resolve with `View`, and answer
  `200 text/plain; charset=utf-8` with `Cache-Control: no-store`. The body is the
  output of `tmux capture-pane -p -S -5000 -E -1`, passed through `tmuxctl.Strip`.
- **FR-015**: `CaptureHistory` MUST refuse, never truncate, output over 5000 lines
  or over 4 MiB, with `ErrHistoryTooLarge`. The route MUST answer that with `500`
  and no body.
- **FR-016**: The page MUST fetch history only when the Scrollback disclosure
  opens. It MUST fetch again on every open, and MUST put the answer into a
  `<pre class="pane">` with `textContent`. An empty answer MUST render "No
  scrollback yet."

### Interface

- **FR-017**: The input panel, the key bar and the Scrollback disclosure MUST be
  rendered inside `partials/pane.html`, after the pane's notes, only when the
  pane has a page token (`{{ with .PageToken }}`). They MUST use only `.button`,
  `.field-label`, `.field-input` and the new classes `.input-panel`, `.type-form`,
  `.key-bar`, `.scrollback`, `.scrollback-summary`.
- **FR-018**: On a coarse pointer, every key-bar button MUST be at least
  `var(--tap)` in both dimensions, and the textarea font MUST be `var(--fs-input)`.
  The key bar MUST be `flex-wrap: wrap`. No new width breakpoint is allowed
  (`TestTheDashboardHasExactlyOneBreakpoint`).
- **FR-019**: The textarea MUST carry `autocapitalize="off" autocorrect="off"
  spellcheck="false"` and a `<label>`. The `.input-panel` MUST be
  `position: sticky; inset-block-end: 0`, so it stays on screen while the pane
  scrolls.
- **FR-020**: The pane note MUST read exactly: "This is the live screen, not
  scrollback. Open Scrollback below to read what came before it." The phrase "not
  scrollback" is pinned by two existing tests.
- **FR-021**: `docs/mobile-open-questions.md` MUST gain Q4 and Q5, both
  **UNANSWERED**, each with its fallback named. Q4 fallback: the key bar becomes a
  second `<details>` ("More keys") holding the arrows, PageUp/PageDown and
  Backspace, with Enter, Esc, Ctrl-C, Tab and Shift-Tab left visible. Q5 fallback:
  move the input panel above the pane.

### Not in this feature

- **FR-022**: No WebSocket, terminal emulator, vendored JavaScript, CSP change,
  API-door input route or change to the stream's 1s cadence. Each one is a
  separate decision with its own review. research.md R6 records why.

**Key Entities**: **Key**, a symbolic name from FR-005's closed set. **Typed
text**, operator bytes that are secret under `docs/security.md` §3, exactly like
prompt text. **History**, the stripped text of tmux's scrollback for one pane,
excluding the visible screen.

## Success Criteria *(mandatory)*

- **SC-001**: `go test ./internal/tmuxctl -tags tmux -run 'Bracketed|History'`
  proves on a real tmux that a two-line bracketed paste arrives wrapped in
  `ESC[200~ … ESC[201~`, and that a 6000-line job yields at most 5000 lines of
  history from a session created by `Exec.New`.
- **SC-002**: The leak suite (`go test ./internal/audit -run Leak`) drives
  `dashboard.type` with a canary string, and the canary appears in no audit
  record and no log line.
- **SC-003**: Every refusal shape that `TestRefusalIsNotARedirect` applies to an
  action is applied to both input routes, and each answers its uniform status.
- **SC-004**: Disabling either route's registration fails a handler test.
- **SC-005**: Q4 and Q5 exist in `docs/mobile-open-questions.md` marked
  UNANSWERED, and nothing in this plan marks them answered.

**Assumptions**: the operator is the only person typing, so arrival order is
good enough and no lock is needed. tmux 3.4 key names are stable across 3.x.
Claude Code 2.1.290 and Codex 0.153.4 both enable bracketed paste. That was
measured, and a later release that stops doing so degrades to "line one
submits", which an operator sees immediately.
